Oral Judgment

(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MOHAMMAD NAWAZ) The insurer of the bus bearing Registration No.KA- 01/AC-3550 has preferred these appeals against the judgment and award dated 03.12.2022 passed in MVC No.610/2019 c/w 611/2019 by the Court of II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Bidar and the judgment and award dated 29.11.2022 passed in MVC No.664/2019 C/w 665/2019 on the file of the Court of Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT,
Bhalki.
2. We have heard the learned counsel Sri S.S.Aspalli appearing for appellant and learned counsel Sri Ganesh Naik appearing for respondents/claimants.

3. MFA No.201513/2023 is preferred against the judgment and award passed in MVC No.664/2019,
MFA No.201416/2023 is preferred against the judgment and award passed in MVC No.665/2019,

MFA No.201434/2023 is preferred against the judgment and award passed in - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3778-DB MVC No.611/2019 and MFA No.201497/2023 is preferred against the judgment and award passed in MVC No.610/2019.

4. The four deceased were traveling in a swift car bearing Reg.No.TS-07/EK-5939 on 04.10.2019 at around 12.30 a.m., when the said car met with an accident on Mumbai-Hyderabad Road near Kala Maruti temple due to head on collision with a bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AC- 3550.

The claimants,
namely the legal heirs of the deceased, filed respective claim petitions before the Tribunal.
The awards passed by the Tribunal are not challenged by the claimants.
However, the Insurer of the bus against whom the liability is fixed by the Tribunal, has filed these appeals.

sentences.text: The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant Sri S.S. Aspalli is that it was a head-on collision between the two vehicles and the claimants in MVC Nos.610/2019 and 611/2019 have admitted that both the - 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3778-DB vehicles are responsible for the accident, hence, the Tribunal was not justified in fixing the liability only on the Insurer of the bus.
In support of his contention, the learned counsel has drawn the attention of the Court to the claim petitions and the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 in MVC Nos.610/2019 and 611/2019.

6. Learned counsel also contended that all the claim petitions arose out of the same accident,
however, the learned Tribunal, in MVC Nos.665/2019 and 664/2019 has awarded interest at the rate of 6% per annum whereas in MVC Nos.610/2019 and 611/2019 has awarded 9% interest.

7. Learned counsel appearing for the respondents, on the other hand, have contended that PW-1 and PW-2 have nowhere stated that the accident was on account of the fault of the driver of the car in which the deceased were traveling and even otherwise, the claimants can claim compensation from one of the tortfeasor as held by - 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3778-DB the Hon'ble Apex Court.

He contended that charge sheet has not been filed against the driver of the car and considering the material placed on record, the Tribunal has rightly fixed the liability to pay the compensation on the appellant/Insurance Company.
8.
We have perused the evidence and material on record.
It is not in dispute that the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AC- 3550.
Admittedly, PW-1 and PW-2, the claimants in MVC No.610/2019 and 611/2019 are not the eyewitnesses to the accident.
They have not specifically stated that the accident was on account of the rash or negligent driving of the driver of the car.
The appellant has not examined any eyewitness to prove that the driver of the car was either solely responsible or there was contributory negligence on his part in causing the accident.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Khenyei vs. New India Assurance Company Limited & others1 has held that in the case of composite negligence, the claimant is entitled to sue both or any of the joint tortfeasor and the entire compensation can be awarded against the sole impleaded tortfeasor.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We find that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal fixing the liability on the appellant to pay the compensation is in accordance with law and does not call for interference.

However, considering the year of accident and in the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that the The Branch Manager vs Madhumati on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119656748/
9 interest to be awarded in all the cases should be 6% per annum.

Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) MFA No.201434/2023 and MFA No.201497/ 2023 are disposed of.

The judgment and award dated 03.12.2022 passed in MVC No.610/2019 C/w MVC No.611/2019 on the (2015) 9 SCC 273 - 14 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3778-DB file of the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Bidar is modified.
The claimants in these petitions are entitled for interest at the rate of 6% per annum instead of 9% awarded by the Tribunal.
(ii) MFA No.201513/2023 and MFA No.201416/ 2023 are dismissed.
The judgment and award dated 29.11.2022 passed in MVC Nos.664 and 665 of 2019 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Bhalki is confirmed.
(iii) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is not in dispute that the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AC- 3550.
They have not specifically stated that the accident was on account of the rash or negligent driving of the driver of the car.
The appellant has not examined any eyewitness to prove that the driver of the car was either solely responsible or there was contributory negligence on his part in causing the accident.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Khenyei vs. New India Assurance Company Limited & others1 has held that in the case of composite negligence, the claimant is entitled to sue both or any of the joint tortfeasor and the entire compensation can be awarded against the sole impleaded tortfeasor.
We find that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal fixing the liability on the appellant to pay the compensation is in accordance with law and does not call for interference.
